column1: # SOURCE: one dated nfl.com article per row, named in source_url. Read via the fetch tool on 2026-11-19 (UTC)
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. The owner's brief lists, as a gap: "Add an announced-starter evidence field (not an
# inferred replacement) — the blank replacement columns are correct for the report page, but the NFL does
# publish dated starter changes for Lock, McCord and Brissett". This file is that field for the three named
# players, built the only way it can be built: by quoting the league's own dated sentence and linking it.
# THE RULE APPLIED. A row exists only where an official nfl.com article states the starter change in words.
# Nothing here is inferred from a depth chart, a jersey number, a practice report, a transaction, or absence
# from the injury report. `statement_as_printed` is a verbatim quotation, not a paraphrase. Where a quotation
# is marked [truncated] the omitted words are shown in `omitted_words`.
# THE DATE IS THE ARTICLE'S PUBLISHED DATE, NOT THIS READ'S DATE. Two dates are recorded: article_date (when
# the league published the statement) and read_at (when this repository read it). They differ by days for
# two of the three rows, and that difference is the whole point of the field: a statement made before
# kickoff is evidence; the same statement read afterwards is only evidence if its date survives.

column4: Drew Lock has no injury designation and will start Sunday for the Seahawks against the host Las Vegas Raiders, coach Mike Macdonald said Friday.
column6: published 2026-11-13 (dated by the article's own 'Nov 13, 2026' listing and its 'said Friday' wording)
column7: head coach, on the record, naming the starter
column12: Lock starts because Sam Darnold is injured; the article names Jalen Milroe as the backup. Week 10 evidence, not Week 11.

column4: With Willis shelved, second-year quarterback Kyle McCord will fill in, beginning Sunday on the road against the Indianapolis Colts.
column6: published 2026-11-10 (the Wednesday before Week 10; the article says Willis was placed on IR 'Tuesday')
column7: club transaction plus named replacement, stated by the league
column12: Malik Willis (groin) to IR; article states he misses Weeks 10-13 and is eligible to return 2026-12-13. McCord is named as the starter, not inferred from the IR move.

column4: NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported ... the Ravens are finalizing a trade for Arizona Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett.
column5: the trade itself is reported, and the starter role is stated only in the secondary headline 'Ravens complete trade for Cardinals' Jacoby Brissett'
column6: published 2026-11-05 or later (trade reported Wednesday, completed Friday)
column7: reported trade (insider), NOT a club announcement of a starter
column12: PARTIAL. This row does NOT satisfy the announced-starter test: the article evidences a trade and an acquisition, not a named starting quarterback. Lamar Jackson was placed on IR (roundup dated 2026-11-05), which makes Brissett the presumptive starter, and that presumption is exactly what the owner's rule forbids publishing as fact. Left as evidence-of-trade with the starter cell blank.
